title: “full ears of corn in the husk thereof” — Brenton’s Greek has “cakes of figs”
summary: The man from Baalshalisha brings Elisha twenty barley loaves and, in the KJV, “full ears of corn in the husk thereof”. The Hebrew word beside the loaves is וְכַרְמֶל בְּצִקְלֹנוֹ; Brenton’s Greek prints καὶ παλάθας, “and cakes of figs”, and has nothing like “in the husk”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 2 Kings 4:42: “And there came a man from Baalshalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 4:42: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנֹ֑ו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃ [and a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought to the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and karmel in his bag/sack; and he said, Give to the people and let them eat]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 4:42: Καὶ ἀνὴρ διῆλθεν ἐκ Βαιθαρισὰ, καὶ ἤνεγκε πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦ Θεοῦ πρωτογεννημάτων εἴκοσι ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ παλάθας· καὶ εἶπε, δότε τῷ λαῷ καὶ ἐσθιέτωσαν. Brenton English: “And there came a man over from Bætharisa, and brought to the man of God twenty barley loaves and cakes of figs, of the first-fruits. And he said, Give to the people, and let them eat.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/4/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI04.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI04.htm.

And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.” Hebrew (WLC) 4:42: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנֹ֑ו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃ Brenton’s Greek 4:42: Καὶ ἀνὴρ διῆλθεν ἐκ Βαιθαρισὰ, καὶ ἤνεγκε πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦ Θεοῦ πρωτογεννημάτων εἴκοσι ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ παλάθας· καὶ εἶπε, δότε τῷ λαῷ καὶ ἐσθιέτωσαν. [and a man came across from Baitharisa, and brought to the man of God, of first fruits, twenty barley loaves and fig cakes; and he said, Give to the people, and let them eat] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/4/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI04.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV renders the Hebrew words כרמל בצקלנו as a grain, “full ears of corn”, with “in the husk thereof” for the following word. Brenton’s Greek names a different food, παλάθας (pressed cakes, here “cakes of figs”), and does not render the Hebrew phrase that the KJV renders “in the husk”. Each text lists a second item beside the barley loaves, but they name different things.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has the barley loaves followed by וְכַרְמֶל בְּצִקְלֹנוֹ, which the KJV renders as ears of corn in a husk (its margin offers “scrip” or “garment”). The Greek printed at the same verse follows the loaves with παλάθας, pressed fig cakes, which names a different food. The KJV and the Greek therefore list different things in addition to the barley loaves.

title: Manasseh “made his son pass through the fire” (Kings) — “his children” (Chronicles); the Greek of Kings has sons
summary: 2 Kings 21:6 says Manasseh made “his son” pass through the fire, one person in the Hebrew (בְּנוֹ). 2 Chronicles 33:6 says “his children” (בָּנָיו), in the valley of the son of Hinnom. Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings 21:6 prints the plural τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, “his sons”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 2 Kings 21:6: “And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 21:6: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת־בְּנֹו֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעֹונֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה אֹ֖וב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ות הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס׃ [and he made his son pass through the fire, and practised soothsaying and divination, and made a ghost-spirit and wizards, and did much evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke him to anger]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 21:6: Καὶ διῆγε τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐν πυρί, καὶ ἐκληδονίζετο καὶ οἰωνίζετο, καὶ ἐποίησε τεμένη, καὶ γνώστας ἐπλήθυνε τοῦ ποιεῖν τὸ πονηρὸν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς Κυρίου παροργίσαι αὐτόν. Brenton English: “And he caused his sons to pass through the fire, and used divination and auspices, and made groves, and multiplied wizards, so as to do that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger..” KJV 2 Chronicles 33:6: “And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Chronicles 33:6: וְהוּא֩ הֶעֱבִ֨יר אֶת־בָּנָ֤יו בָּאֵשׁ֙ בְּגֵ֣י בֶן־הִנֹּ֔ם וְעֹונֵ֤ן וְנִחֵשׁ֙ וְֽכִשֵּׁ֔ף וְעָ֥שָׂה אֹ֖וב וְיִדְּעֹונִ֑י הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ות הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֹֽו׃ Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI21.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/21/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI21.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI21.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH33.htm and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/33/.

KJV 2 Kings 21:6: “And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.” Hebrew (WLC) 21:6: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת־בְּנֹו֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעֹונֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה אֹ֖וב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ות הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס׃ Brenton’s Greek 21:6: Καὶ διῆγε τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐν πυρί, καὶ ἐκληδονίζετο καὶ οἰωνίζετο, καὶ ἐποίησε τεμένη, καὶ γνώστας ἐπλήθυνε τοῦ ποιεῖν τὸ πονηρὸν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς Κυρίου παροργίσαι αὐτόν. [and he made his sons pass through fire, and used omens and bird-signs, and made sacred precincts, and multiplied diviners, to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI21.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/21/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI21.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV follows the Hebrew in both books: the singular בְּנוֹ in Kings and the plural בָּנָיו in Chronicles. Brenton’s Greek of Kings prints the plural τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, which agrees with the Chronicles Hebrew and differs from the Kings Hebrew in number. A reader of the KJV sees one son in Kings and several children in Chronicles; a reader of the Greek of Kings sees several in both.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has a singular noun with the possessive ending: his son. The Greek printed at the same verse has the plural noun with the article: his sons. The KJV and the Hebrew name one child; the Greek names more than one.

title: Sennacherib’s sons escaped into “the land of Armenia” — the Hebrew prints “the land of Ararat”
summary: In both 2 Kings 19:37 and Isaiah 37:38 the KJV says Adrammelech and Sharezer escaped “into the land of Armenia”. The Hebrew prints אֶרֶץ אֲרָרָט, “the land of Ararat”, a different name, and Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings prints Ararath. Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings 19:37 also prints Ἀραράθ, so the Greek agrees with the Hebrew against the KJV there. At Isaiah 37:38 Brenton instead prints Ἀρμενίαν (Armenia), agreeing with the KJV; only the Hebrew differs there.
text: KJV 2 Kings 19:37: “And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Armenia. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 19:37: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית ׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר (בָּנָיו֙  ק) הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃  פ [and it happened, as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat; and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 19:37: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ προσκυνοῦντος ἐν οἴκῳ Μεσερὰχ τοῦ θεοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ἀδραμέλεχ καὶ Σαρασὰρ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπάταξαν αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρᾳ· καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσώθησαν εἰς γῆν Ἀραράθ· καὶ ἐβασίλευσεν Ἀσορδὰν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἀντʼ αὐτοῦ. KJV Isaiah 37:38: “And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.” Hebrew (WLC) Isaiah 37:38: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא  מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית ׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃    ס Brenton English 2 Kings 19:37: “And it came to pass, while he was worshipping in the house of Meserach his god, that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Ararath; and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI19.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/19/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI19.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI19.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ISA37.htm and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/37/.
reasoning: The KJV puts the later regional name “Armenia” where both Hebrew verses print the name אֲרָרָט (Ararat), with אֶרֶץ, “land”. The Hebrew text has no word that reads “Armenia”; Brenton’s Greek transliterates Ararath at 2 Kings 19:37, but has Armenia at Isaiah 37:38. A reader of the KJV alone does not see that the verse names Ararat, the name the KJV prints in Genesis 8:4 for the mountains where the ark rested.

The two names may point to the same region: the KJV’s “Armenia” can be a modern-for-ancient substitution, and this record does not say the KJV places the sons in the wrong country or that Ararat and Armenia are different places. title: An ass’s head at “fourscore pieces of silver” — Brenton’s Greek says fifty
summary: During the siege of Samaria the KJV says an ass’s head sold for “fourscore pieces of silver”. The Hebrew prints בִּשְׁמֹנִים כֶּסֶף, eighty of silver; Brenton’s Greek prints πεντήκοντα ἀργυρίου, fifty of silver. The price of the dove’s dung, five pieces, agrees.
text: KJV 2 Kings 6:25: “And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 6:25: וַיְהִ֨י רָעָ֤ב גָּדֹול֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְרֹ֔ון וְהִנֵּ֖ה צָרִ֣ים עָלֶ֑יהָ עַ֣ד הֱיֹ֤ות רֹאשׁ־חֲמֹור֙ בִּשְׁמֹנִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף וְרֹ֛בַע הַקַּ֥ב [חֲרֵייֹונִים כ] (דִּבְיֹונִ֖ים  ק) בַּחֲמִשָּׁה־כָֽסֶף׃ [and there was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, besieging it, until the head of a donkey was at eighty of silver, and the fourth of a qab of dove’s dung/pods at five of silver]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 6:25: Καὶ ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐν Σαμαρείᾳ· καὶ ἰδοὺ περιεκάθηντο ἐπʼ αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἐγενήθη κεφαλὴ ὄνου πεντήκοντα ἀργυρίου, καὶ τέταρτον τοῦ κάβου κόπρου περιστερῶν πέντε ἀργυρίου. [… until the head of a donkey was fifty of silver, and a fourth of a qab of doves’ dung five of silver]. Brenton English: “And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was valued at fifty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung at five pieces of silver.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI06.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI06.htm.
reasoning: The KJV’s “fourscore” is eighty and matches the Hebrew word שְׁמֹנִים. Brenton’s Greek has the word for fifty. The two texts print different numbers for the same price in the same verse, so a reader who follows the Greek tradition reads a cheaper head than a reader of the Hebrew.
scope: T applies at 2 Kings 6:25, Septuagint only. The KJV agrees with the Hebrew, and no Hebrew mistranslation is claimed. The record states two printed numbers and does not say which is original or that either is wrong, and it makes no claim about the market price of any item. The Hebrew marks the word for the second item with a written form and a read form (חֲרֵייֹונִים, דִּבְיֹונִים); that is not the point of this record and is not compared. title: The scouts sent after the Syrians: “two chariot horses” — Brenton’s Greek says two horsemen
summary: In the KJV the king’s servants take “two chariot horses” and send them after the Syrian army. Brenton’s Greek prints δύο ἐπιβάτας ἵππων, “two horsemen”, riders on horses, where the KJV has animals drawing a chariot.
text: KJV 2 Kings 7:14: “They took therefore two chariot horses; and the king sent after the host of the Syrians, saying, Go and see.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 7:14: וַיִּקְח֕וּ שְׁנֵ֖י רֶ֣כֶב סוּסִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֧י מַחֲנֵֽה־אֲרָ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר לְכ֥וּ וּרְאֽוּ׃ [and they took two of chariot of horses, and the king sent after the camp of Aram, saying, Go and see]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 7:14: Καὶ ἔλαβον δύο ἐπιβάτας ἵππων· καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ ὀπίσω τοῦ βασιλέως Συρίας, λέγων, δεῦτε, καὶ ἴδετε. Brenton English: “So they took two horsemen; and the king of Israel sent after the king of Syria, saying, Go, and see.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI07.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI07.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI07.htm.
reasoning: The KJV’s “two chariot horses” follows the Hebrew שְׁנֵי רֶכֶב סוּסִים, which has the word רֶכֶב (chariotry, chariot) and the word for horses. Brenton’s Greek has ἐπιβάτας, a word for those who mount or ride, and the English renders it “horsemen”. The KJV’s two are animals; the Greek’s two are men on horses.
scope: T applies at 2 Kings 7:14, Septuagint only. The record does not claim that the KJV mistranslates the Hebrew and does not say how many men went, or whether the two chariots or two riders are meant; the Hebrew phrase is compressed and the record states only the two printed wordings. The five horses of 7:13 are in both texts and are not compared here. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.

title: “The child sneezed seven times” — Brenton’s Greek prints that Elisha bowed himself over the child seven times
summary: In the KJV of 2 Kings 4:35 the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Brenton’s Greek prints καὶ ἀνέβη καὶ συνέκαμψεν ἐπὶ τὸ παιδάριον ἕως ἑπτάκις, “and he went up and bent himself over the child up to seven times”, where the Hebrew edition quoted has וַיְזֹורֵר הַנַּעַר עַד־שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים, “and the boy sneezed seven times”.
text: KJV 2 Kings 4:35: “Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.” Hebrew (WLC) 4:35: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּבַּ֗יִת אַחַ֥ת הֵ֙נָּה֙ וְאַחַ֣ת הֵ֔נָּה וַיַּ֖עַל וַיִּגְהַ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיְזֹורֵ֤ר הַנַּ֙עַר֙ עַד־שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּפְקַ֥ח הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־עֵינָֽיו׃ Brenton’s Greek 4:35: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψε, καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν· καὶ ἀνέβη καὶ συνέκαμψεν ἐπὶ τὸ παιδάριον ἕως ἑπτάκις· καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ παιδάριον τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ. [and he returned and walked in the house this way and that; and he went up and bent himself over the child up to seven times; and the child opened his eyes] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/4/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI04.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has the boy as the subject of the verb וַיְזֹורֵר, which the KJV renders “sneezed”. The Greek printed at the same verse has the man bending over the child seven times and no verb for the child’s sneeze. The seven times belong to the child in the KJV and to the prophet in the Greek.
scope: T applies at 2 Kings 4:35 only. The record does not say what the Hebrew verb זרר means and does not claim the KJV’s “sneezed” is certain. It does not compare 4:34. It does not say what the Greek translators or later copyists intended. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. title: “Hast thou not heard long ago how I have done it” — Brenton’s Greek prints “I formed it, I gathered it”
summary: In the KJV of 2 Kings 19:25 the Lord asks Sennacherib whether he has not heard long ago what the Lord did. Brenton’s Greek prints only Ἔπλασα αὐτήν, συνήγαγον αὐτήν, “I formed it, I gathered it”, and does not print the question or the words “long ago”.
text: KJV 2 Kings 19:25: “Hast thou not heard long ago how I have done it, and of ancient times that I have formed it? now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste fenced cities into ruinous heaps.” Hebrew (WLC) 19:25: הֲלֹֽא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחֹוק֙ אֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי לְמִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִֽיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵיאתִ֗יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לַהְשֹׁ֛ות גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֹֽות׃ Brenton’s Greek 19:25: Ἔπλασα αὐτὴν, συνήγαγον αὐτήν· καὶ ἐγενήθη εἰς ἐπάρσεις ἀποικεσιῶν μαχίμων πόλεις ὀχυράς. [I formed it, I gathered it; and it became cities, strong ones, as a raising up of the captivities of warriors] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI19.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/19/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI19.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted opens with a question, הֲלֹא־שָׁמַעְתָּ, “have you not heard”, and says the Lord made it from far-off days and formed it. The Greek printed at the same verse has two verbs spoken by the Lord, formed and gathered, and no question, no “heard” and no “long ago”. The KJV text asks the king whether he has heard; the Greek states what the Lord did.
scope: T applies at 2 Kings 19:25 only. The record does not compare the second half of the verse, where the sentence about fortified cities reads differently in the two texts, and does not claim the Hebrew and the Greek are two forms of the same sentence.
